label: Corn
risk_note: Highest water and nitrogen demand; yield most sensitive to water stress from tasseling through silking (mid–late July)
source: Water use 24–30 in (KS), USDA-RMA 2006 from K-State/UNL bulletins; threshold ET 10.9 in and silking sensitivity, Stone & Schlegel (K-State) 2006; rooting 5–6 ft, UW-Madison Agronomy

label: Soybean
risk_note: Low residue after harvest leaves soil exposed; sensitive to drought during pod set and early bean fill (August)
source: Water use 18–24 in (KS), USDA-RMA 2006; threshold ET 9.0 in and critical stages, Stone & Schlegel (K-State) 2006

label: Grain sorghum
risk_note: Crops planted right after sorghum (especially fall-sown winter grains or cover crops) may establish poorly; sugarcane aphid; confirm local elevator market
source: Water use 18–22 in (KS), USDA-RMA 2006; threshold ET 6.9 in, Stone & Schlegel 2006; heat & drought tolerance, resistance to corn rootworm/borer, 3–4 ft roots, and crop-after-sorghum caution, UW-Madison Agronomy

label: Winter wheat
risk_note: Needs a fall planting window after the summer crop; Hessian fly and rust risk; vulnerable to late spring freeze (e.g. April 2007)
source: Water use 16–18 in (NE), USDA-RMA 2006; measured 19.0 in at Manhattan KS, Kanemasu (K-State) 1977; season temporally displaced from summer demand, Lamm (K-State) 2014; root depth 1.5 m = FAO-56 Table 22 maximum effective rooting depth (1.5–1.8 m), a literature reference value, not a local measurement — the model uses min(this, inferred claypan limit); was 1.2 m (audit item 17)

label: Double-crop soybean
risk_note: Only works if mid-summer rain is adequate after wheat harvest; lower yield than full-season soybean
source: Shorter season than full-season soybean (same physiology as soybean row); local agronomist to confirm

label: Alfalfa (hay)
risk_note: Very high water use; poorly suited to wet, slow-draining clay subsoil; needs a hay market or livestock
source: Water use 34–36 in (eastern NE), USDA-RMA 2006; 20–46 in, Dey, Jha & Min (K-State) 2024; roots extract water to ~8 ft, Stone et al. (K-State) 1982

label: Sunflower
risk_note: Limited local market in Riley County; bird damage
source: Water use 22 in (KS), USDA-RMA 2006; threshold ET 5.4 in (most drought-tolerant summer crop), Stone & Schlegel 2006

label: Oats
risk_note: Small local grain market; best as forage or nurse crop
source: General agronomy; local agronomist to confirm

label: Cereal rye cover crop
risk_note: Before corn: terminate early (rye under ~8 in, ≥2 weeks before planting) to limit nitrogen tie-up — K-State recommends rye mainly before soybean; in a dry spring it uses moisture the next crop needs; seed and seeding cost; host of wheat streak mosaic virus and wheat curl mite (risk near wheat); after sorghum, establishment can be poor
source: Termination rule of thumb, University of Minnesota Extension 2025; slow N release, Sievers & Cook, SSSAJ 2018; planting by Nov 1 for most of Kansas, N scavenging, erosion and evaporation reduction, wheat streak mosaic virus host risk, K-State Agronomy eUpdate 'Planting cereal rye after corn harvest' and K-State MF3504; water use 120 mm is an ASSUMPTION consistent with Nebraska on-farm data (0 to 3.4 in less profile water at soybean planting, usually refilled after planting; Upper Big Blue NRD)

label: Hairy vetch cover crop
risk_note: Releases >70% of its nitrogen within two weeks of termination, so time termination close to planting; seed cost; can become a weed in wheat
source: Sievers & Cook, Soil Sci. Soc. Am. J. 82(1):147, 2018; UNL CropWatch 2023
